newsitem.title: ITALY: Soccer-Vicenza's foreign owners say it could float.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Vicenza's foreign owners say it could float.

text.p: The managing director of the British firm Stelican, which became Italy's first foreign soccer club owner by buying serie A side Vicenza, said on Friday the club could list on the stock exchange.
"The club has been in profit for three consecutive years. It could be a candidate for flotation in Italy," Stelican managing director Stephen Julius said.

Stellican, an investment firm which specialises in buying out destressed companies and is closely linked to U.S. investment group Apollo, bought Vicenza last week from a bankruptcy court for 22.75 billion lire ($13.5 million).

Vicenza, which was promoted to serie A in 1995 and qualified for next season's European Cup Winners' Cup, has a profitable balance sheet but was put into receivership as a result of bankruptcy affecting the owners.
Julius said Vicenza was a bargain compared to English Premier League clubs, many of which had already floated succesfully on the London stock market.
"It was a sensible price. An attractive price if you look at publically quoted English football clubs," he said after meeting Vicenza management on Friday.

Julius, who is half Italian himself, said that Stellican had faced some opposition from people in Vicenza after it won the bid last Friday but added that initial fears that a foreign takeover would be unpopular with local fans had evaporated.

"In the one week between making the bid and being called to the court...the mayor was getting a bit nationalistic," he said, referring to comments by city mayor Marino Quaresimin that Stellican's performance would be closely watched.

"(The British angle) is a non-issue now. The people in Vicenza might have wanted a local asset in local hands but that didn't happen. Now I think there's a lot of curiosity in an English group to see what they can do," he said.
Julius said Stellican would not touch the management structure at Vicenza, adding he had "developed a close working relationship" with the club's director general Sergio Gasparin.
He said the firm would concentrate on increasing the club's revenue in television and sponsorship rights as well as developing the merchandising sector.

Julius said he would focus on pay-per-view television by asking the Italain soccer federation, which carves up profits through a share system, to increase Vicenza's quota from two to four shares worth 1.4 billion lire each.
Stellican's acquisition of Vicenza could pave the way for further foreign takeovers of Italian clubs, Julius said, adding that the intense interest in the whole issue had surprised him.
"This is a medium-sized company. It's not the world's biggest deal," he said. "The media coverage has really taken our breath away."
